description: On January 1, 1923, the new Maya artifact exhibition hall at the British Museum opened. Professor Smith invited the investigators to visit. The relief depicting blood sacrifices and the tradition of the god-king foretell horror.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: A new story begins, wish you all a pleasant journey! Recording of the horror on the Orient Express has now commenced... Wait, a piece of paper flew out... Even the five-star critic MacArthur couldn't help but sigh.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: So, the time is Monday, January 1, 1923. Invited by Professor Smith, three members of Miskatonic University have traveled thousands of miles across the Atlantic to London, England. You arrived here two days before the Challenger Lecture begins, and now you are standing in the British Museum with Professor Smith. On January 1, 1923, the British Museum opened a new exhibition hall including the Maudslay Collection, featuring ancient stone carvings from early Maya tribes in southern Mexico and Central America. Professor Smith hopes you can spend two days familiarizing yourselves with the city and attend his lecture on the third day. Hmm, coincidentally, a new exhibition hall opened on January 1st. So you are here to visit and incidentally get to know each other.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #The first stop is an English-speaking country, a good time for slacking off has arrived.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "In the 1880s, archaeologist Dr. Alfred P. Maudslay discovered these stone carvings from ruined jungle temples during his expeditions. Now, these antiquities are being opened to the public for exhibition." Professor Smith introduces this new exhibition hall to you.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #A look of awe.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: You can see many jungle artifacts, stone carvings, stone pillars, and tools used by primitive people inside the exhibition hall. "Oh, you haven't met each other yet, let me introduce you."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "The boss would be very interested." #Gesturing to Professor Bailan beside him, although he doesn't pay the salary.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: @player7 "This is Mr. Gungnir, the spokesperson for the Rhode Island Yellow Book Society." (Huh? Smith is introducing (0)

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Frowning "Professor, don't be so blunt."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Hmm, okay?" Professor Smith feels a bit awkward.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Anyway," #Hands hanging down "It's not good to expose that you're also a heavy user."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Haha...."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Hello everyone, I am a medical student from Miskatonic University. I am honored to be invited by Mr. Smith to attend the lecture, and I am very pleased to meet you all."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "A talented young person, pleased to meet you."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: (Bailan isn't from the Yellow Book Society (0)

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "It's an honor to meet you all here." #Nodding politely, extending a hand to shake with everyone, with a gentle yet courteous smile.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Shake hands with Bailan in a friendly manner.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Extend a hand and shake Bailan's hand.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "player4 - Durgan and... Bailan - Sha" Professor Smith nods as he introduces.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Just call me player4, Professor Smith."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Thank you very much for coming from afar. Please enjoy the city properly these two days." "London is a very beautiful city." Then he leads you inside. In the center of the exhibition hall, several fragments of Maya lintels from the 4th-6th centuries AD are displayed. The reliefs on them, though weathered for millennia, still clearly show intricate ritual scenes.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "That's right, I was fortunate enough to have been here before. It truly is a very beautiful place. I still remember the past by the River Thames." #Then follows inside.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Follows the professor inside, idly looking around at the exhibits.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Cool-toned light falls upon the ancient relics carved from limestone and obsidian.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Oh... Professor Bailan is really well-traveled and knowledgeable."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The most eye-catching is a limestone lintel from the Palenque ruins. The relief on it depicts a solemn and bloody bloodletting ritual—a noble wearing a feathered headdress holds an obsidian dagger, piercing his own tongue, blood dripping onto a bark paper scroll; at his feet, a captive is bound kneeling, eyes vacant, with sacrificial symbols carved on the neck. The nearby display panel explains: "The Maya believed that blood was the link between the divine realm and the human world, and the sacrifice of captives was a sacred feast offered to the gods." In glass cases on both sides of the hall, small stone carvings and pottery figurines are displayed.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Internally ranting about how this damp, hot city environment mixed with fog and industrial exhaust can also be shamelessly called beautiful.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The professor examines these collections with great interest.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Frowning upon seeing such a bloody and cruel ritual.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Eyes sweep over these ancient artifacts "Live sacrifice, communication with the gods."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Hmm... There is the title 'k'uhul ajaw' on the lintel edge. This ritual might... be related to the 'Divine King Blood Sacrifice' tradition in Maya kingship mythology." Professor Smith analyzed while taking notes in his notebook.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Watching the exhibits expressionlessly, not particularly shocked by such a bloody scene.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: After about an hour of browsing, you have finished touring this exhibition hall.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "What is Divine King Blood Sacrifice? Is it about pleading for answers from ancient gods?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: (Can make an Archaeology roll)

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "It's alright, Professor. Please attend to your own matters."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Then Professor Smith recommends a cost-effective hotel to you.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Then Bailan can analyze that these offerings were used for deities to consume, to bless the ruler's life and rebirth.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Watching these history experts babble here like a Muggle.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "So, shall we stay together? That way we can look out for each other."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Briefly explain to companions about this bizarre, bloody ritual.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #player2 nods to player4. "The boss said accommodation expenses can be reimbursed."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "!! That's great!"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: London's sunset slowly sinks into the River Thames. Twilight coats the spires of the British Museum with a layer of dark gold. The river surface shimmers with rust-colored ripples. Barges and steam ferries trail long plumes of coal smoke. Gas lamps along the streets light up one after another, their dim yellow halos seeping into the thin mist.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I think so too. Having a generous boss is really great." #player2 sways his short upper body in agreement with your statement.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: You are very tired after the long journey.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #The college student who already lacks exercise decides to sleep.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #As a country bumpkin who grew up and lived in Rhode Island, expresses dissatisfaction with England's heavily industrialized and polluted environment by coughing.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: @player8

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Slee~p

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: January 2, 1923. The chill in London has not yet dissipated. player5, wrapped in an overcoat, stops before an old bookstall, fingers brushing over a yellowed South American expedition notebook; player4 prays in a London church; while player2 silently follows behind them, eyes vigilantly scanning the crowd as if ready to deal with invisible threats at any moment. They have afternoon tea at a tearoom in Russell Square. Bailan talks about nightmares of the rainforest, player4 listens with a smile, while player2 just silently stirs the sugar cubes. As dusk falls, the three stroll along the Thames embankment. The halos of gas lamps shatter into golden ripples on the river surface. In the distance, the dull chime of Big Ben marking the hour can be heard.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Sits up straight.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "The reason I use the term 'associated phenomenon' is because those haunted things do not occur only for a specific observer. As we have seen, hauntings can happen whether there are human witnesses or not. Therefore, human perception of such phenomena is secondary to the phenomenon itself."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #In my seat, like a student in a public lecture, utterly bored but having to put on an attentive face, actually just thinking about when we can eat.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Listening seriously while thinking. After all, having seen many bizarre things, one always maintains some vigilance.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Recalling knowledge seen in the library, nodding thoughtfully.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Bailan felt the back of her head being brushed by hair, which interrupted her train of thought.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Looking back

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Then you see a man behind you, about under forty years old, with such a thick beard that you would mentally categorize him as a 'foreigner.' He was passing behind you and accidentally bumped into you. Seeing you look back, he made an apologetic gesture and hurried away.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hmm..." #Silently watching where this person disappears to

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: That person disappeared at the exit.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: (Are you typing, or waiting for me to RP?)

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Then the challenger's speech ended, and everyone dispersed.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Walking over to Bailan and player4

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "No... I was listening to the speech the whole time."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "No, just met a strange person."
